sources.title: Asian Development Bank investigation report: Sindh cultural heritage appendix
sources.note: Institutional investigation summarizing disputed Soomra chronology, the Dodo-Chanesar tradition, and Tharri as an attributed but unexcavated early capital.

sources.title: Saints of the Indus: The Rise of Islam in South Asia’s Borderlands
sources.note: Peer-reviewed regional synthesis used to bound political and religious change in the lower Indus borderlands.

sources.title: Port of Banbhore
sources.note: UNESCO state-party archaeological account of a fortified port, reservoir, industries, imports, and Indian Ocean exchange.

sources.title: The Soomras of Sindh
sources.note: University of Karachi-hosted regional reconstruction with an explicit proposed ruler sequence; used as one reconstruction, never as settled chronology.

sources.title: The Sumras in The History of India as Told by Its Own Historians
sources.note: Digitized historical discussion emphasizing late, inconsistent sources, uncertain lineage and duration, and limited rather than absolute authority.

sources.title: Soomra period historical discussion
sources.note: Sindhi Language Authority-hosted discussion exposing contradictory names, dates, and successions in later narratives.

sources.title: An Illustrated Historical Atlas of the Soomra Kingdom of Sindh
sources.note: Regional historical atlas used only for attributed reconstructions of centers and ruler chronology, with uncertainty retained.

sources.title: Al-Idrisi on Sind in The History of India, volume 1
sources.note: Digitized translation of al-Idrisi’s c.1154 compilation describing Debal and Mansura houses, markets, foods, clothing, coins, shipping, and trade.

sources.title: Arabic text and study of al-Idrisi’s Nuzhat al-mushtaq
sources.note: Scholarly PDF containing the exact Arabic sentence used for the written-language sample.

sources.title: Bibliothèque nationale de France authority record for al-Idrisi
sources.note: National-library authority record supporting author, Arabic work, and twelfth-century date.

sources.title: Al-Idrisi and the Nuzhat al-mushtaq
sources.note: Scholarly preview explaining al-Idrisi’s Sicily-based compilation method and the limits of treating it as local eyewitness testimony.

sources.title: The Indus Delta and the Rann of Kutch
sources.note: Peer-reviewed historical geography on changing channels, delta silting, and the formation of salt-marsh landscapes.

sources.title: Early medieval India: Arab Sind and regional contacts
sources.note: University course unit on multilingual contacts, translation, and regional political and commercial networks.

sources.title: Ghurids
sources.note: Encyclopaedia Iranica chronology for Ghurid activity at Multan and Uch in 1175 and lower-Sind Sumeras acknowledging suzerainty in 1182.

sources.title: Soomras of Sind in The New Islamic Dynasties
sources.note: Online text of Bosworth’s chronological manual, used for broad dynastic continuation beyond 1200 rather than exact local reigns.

sources.title: The period of Arab rule in Sind: urban development and architecture
sources.note: UNESCO urban-history chapter on Banbhore and Mansura plans, houses, streets, defenses, mosques, civic buildings, water, and industries.

sources.title: Banbhore Fort, Thatta
sources.note: Government of Sindh site record locating the fortified port on an old Indus channel and noting its long archaeological sequence.

sources.title: Archaeological Museum Banbhore
sources.note: Government museum inventory of storage jars, glass, glazed wares, and Chinese pottery from broad site phases.

sources.title: Brahmanabad or Mansura
sources.note: Government of Sindh summary of the ruins, excavation history, coins, jewelry, and other objects recovered at Mansura.

sources.title: Banbhore archaeological project
sources.note: Research-center report on locally made and imported materials, Indian Ocean links, and thousands of worked ivory, bone, and shell fragments.

sources.title: Glass finds from Banbhore
sources.note: University of Bologna research record on glass assemblages and compositional study of technologies and exchange links.

sources.title: History and archaeology at Banbhore and Lower Sindh
sources.note: Scholarly synthesis on production, redistribution, ivory and bone waste, glass, metallurgy, mother-of-pearl, and imported porcelains.

sources.title: Islamic South Asian archaeology: Banbhore and Mansura
sources.note: Archaeological synthesis detailing residences, wells, covered drains, workshops, baths, and possible mosque-side latrine channels.

sources.title: Mansura excavation diary, Muhammad Sharif, 1966
sources.note: Government excavation index recording rooms, food remains, toys, children’s teeth, bathing tub, drainpipe, soak pit, ornaments, and weapons in mixed layers.

sources.title: Mansura excavation diary, Makin Khan, 1977 to 1978
sources.note: Government field record indexing residential rooms, veranda, courtyard, water supply, terracotta pipe, drain, rubbish, toys, and stratigraphy.

sources.title: Mansura excavation diary, Shams Din Jatoi, 1981
sources.note: Government field record indexing wheat, bones, a cooking furnace, storage jar, copper bowl, weights, bangles, and structural phases.

sources.title: Mansura excavation diary, Mazhar Ali, 1982
sources.note: Government field record indexing fish and bird bones, eggshell, date palm, grinding stone, toys, weapons, covered drain, soak pit, and rubbish pits.

sources.title: Six Thousand Years of Irrigation in Sindh
sources.note: Specialist regional history of inundation channels and shifting Indus cultivation, treated as reconstruction rather than measured medieval acreage.

sources.title: The Cultural Heritage of Pakistan
sources.note: Academic cultural history on Arabic, Sindhi, and other linguistic traditions and written culture in the lower Indus region.

sources.title: Trials and Tribulations in the Dodo-Chanesar oral epic
sources.note: Academic oral-literature study finding no documented version of the Dodo-Chanesar epic before the seventeenth century.

sources.title: Education IV: The Medieval Madrasa
sources.note: Encyclopaedia Iranica account of medieval madrasa institutions, used only as comparative background and not proof of a school at a named Sindh site.

sources.title: Muslim educational institutions in Uch
sources.note: Academic article dating a named Uch madrasa to 1206 to 1222, after the atlas endpoint, and therefore documenting a limit rather than period evidence.

sources.title: Ancient City of Qalhat nomination dossier: Indian Ocean ports comparison
sources.note: UNESCO comparative dossier describing Banbhore’s occupation and exchange sequence as continuing into the thirteenth century.

scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.

Agent researched a disjoint batch; integration and structural checks are not independent historical certification.
Imported border coordinates remain unchanged. Historical events and map coverage are distinguished in prose; see batchIdentityNotes for conflicts.

proposedOverrides.summary: Lower-Indus dynasty card with disputed chronology and an exact atlas seam.

batchIdentityNotes: The exact Soomra Emirate polygon is a generated editorial layer, not a surveyed dynasty border or the modern province of Sindh.
The card keeps Mansura, Banbhore, textual Debal, Tharri, Multan, and wider lower-Sind evidence localized and separately qualified.
Later ruler lists and the Dodo-Chanesar epic are not treated as contemporary chronicles; competing chronologies remain visible.
The exact id disappears at 1200 while historical reconstructions continue Soomra rule, so fell remains null and no single successor is invented.
